title: Two tabs, one document
fullTitle: Two Tabs. One Document. Where Did My Changes Go?

captions.text: Tab A saves a new title: 200 OK.
Tab B saves. The old title is back. No error anywhere.
Two independent clients load the same document at version 1.
Separate sessions in a local test, not real browsers.
A edits the title. B edits only the body.
B's copy still holds the old title, and saving sends everything.
The flawed update only asks: does the ID match?
Nothing asks which version B was looking at. Last writer wins.
One atomic UPDATE: match id AND version, replace, increment.
Check rows changed. Never a separate read, then write.
A saves against version 1: 200, now version 2.
B sends version 1, matches no row: 409 with the current version.
B's unsaved text is kept. Both versions are shown.
A person resolves it. No automatic merge, no overwrite retry.
Only a version mismatch is a 409. A locked database is a 503.
Two racing saves, same version: exactly one is accepted.
Conflict detection, not real-time collaboration, not a CRDT.
Before saving, check what you are replacing.
